negative_findings.description: No SK acquirer or PSP was found publishing a regular, structured statistical release of its own transaction volumes, merchant counts or average ticket. Disclosures are one-off marketing claims embedded in prose (e.g. SKPAY '28,000+ POS terminals', Global Payments '37,000+ terminals in Slovakia', Comgate '21,000+ merchants', GoPay '7,000+ merchants', Besteron '1,500+ e-shops').
negative_findings.result_summary: Merchant/terminal figures exist only as scattered, undated marketing sentences; no acquirer-published time series.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Any acquirer-level time series for SK must be reconstructed by snapshotting corporate pages over time and by text-mining statutory annual reports — it cannot be pulled from a publisher-maintained dataset.

negative_findings.description: Searched in Slovak for softPOS merchant adoption numbers (softPOS Slovensko, platobný terminál v mobile, počet obchodníkov). Found that SLSP, ČSOB, Tatra banka and VÚB all offer phone-as-terminal products, and general aggregates (mobile payments = 22% of card transactions; cashless = 55% of transactions; 16 terminals per 1,000 inhabitants vs EU 32), but no provider-level softPOS merchant counts.
negative_findings.result_summary: SoftPOS adoption in SK is documented qualitatively and by bank product launches, not by published merchant counts.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: SoftPOS is the main mechanism closing SK's terminal-density gap; without provider-level counts, coverage growth can only be inferred from SBA/ZBK aggregate acceptance-point statistics.

negative_findings.description: The Slovenská FinTech asociácia member list could not be located in search results; only the association's homepage, Facebook page and FinStat/Transparex entity records surfaced. A second association (FINAS) exists but its membership was likewise not visible from search snippets.
negative_findings.result_summary: No public membership directory confirmed for either SK fintech association.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Association memberships are the cheapest way to enumerate small non-bank payment actors; if they are not public, the actor map must lean entirely on the NBS PSD2 register plus press snowballing.

negative_findings.description: No settled Slovak-language term was found for 'acquirer' as an institution type. SK material uses circumlocutions — 'akceptácia platobných kariet', 'prijímanie platobných kariet', 'poskytovateľ platobných terminálov', 'zúčtovacia banka' — while English 'acquiring' appears mainly in EN-language corporate material.
negative_findings.result_summary: Acquiring is described functionally, not named, in Slovak sources.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Query design must use the functional Slovak phrases rather than a literal translation of 'acquirer', or local sources will be systematically missed.

negative_findings.description: The brand 'TrustPay' returns heavy SEO spam from gambling/betting affiliate sites (e.g. trustpaystavky.com) that impersonate payment-provider guides. Similarly 'platobná brána' returns mostly affiliate comparison blogs rather than provider primary sources.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two core query terms are polluted by affiliate content.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Automated collection on these terms will ingest low-credibility affiliate pages; domain allowlisting to provider and register domains is required.

negative_findings.description: Two URLs in the candidate list were inferred rather than observed in search results: the NBS PSD2 JSON endpoint https://subjekty.nbs.sk/api/psd2 (reported in a search summary, not fetched by me) and https://www.besteron.sk/ (constructed from the brand name). Both are hypotheses pending the deterministic liveness pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Two URLs unconfirmed; not fabricated facts but unverified addresses.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The PSD2 JSON endpoint is the single highest-leverage automation target in this cell; if it does not exist in that form, the HTML register must be parsed instead.

coverage_gaps.description: Card scheme SK-country outputs (Visa CEE / Mastercard Slovakia country press and 'Slovensko platí kartou' style campaigns) were not directly enumerated in this pass, though a VÚB campaign referencing 'Slovakia Pays by Card' surfaced indirectly. Schemes are the usual original source behind SK terminal-density and contactless-share figures quoted by the press.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass on visa.sk / mastercard.com/sk-sk newsrooms and on the 'Slovensko platí kartou' campaign to reach the primary numbers behind SITA/ZBK reporting.

coverage_gaps.description: No cross-check was made against ECB Payments Statistics / NBS payment statistics tables (Štatistika platobného styku), which report SK acquiring-side counts (POS terminals, acceptance points, card transactions at terminals located in SK) on a harmonised basis. This is the authoritative denominator against which every acquirer's self-reported estate should be normalised.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add NBS statistical publications and the ECB SDW payments dataset (country=SK) as a separate baseline source before relying on any vendor-reported terminal count.

coverage_gaps.description: Crypto/e-money hybrids and BNPL providers active in SK (e.g. Fumbi-type EMIs, Twisto/Skip Pay-style BNPL, Revolut Bank's SK merchant activity) were not covered, nor were payroll/expense-card EMIs. These hold e-money licences and appear in the NBS register but sit outside classic card acquiring.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate the full NBS PSD2/e-money register and classify each entity by business model before assuming the acquiring-centric actor list is complete.

coverage_gaps.description: Interchange Fee Regulation (IFR) Article 9/12 disclosures — acquirers' published merchant service charge and scheme-fee breakdowns — were not located for SK acquirers, although Global Payments' 'dôležité dokumenty' and SKPAY's 'obchodné podmienky' PDFs are the likely carriers.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Systematically harvest T&C and fee-schedule PDFs from every SK acquirer's document page; these give per-transaction economics that no statistical release provides.

coverage_gaps.description: All searching was done in Slovak and English as required. Czech-language sources were only encountered incidentally (paytenpos.cz, Comgate) despite the CZ/SK payments market being operationally integrated — many SK-relevant PSP disclosures are published only in Czech.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add Czech (cs) as a third search language for this cell, targeting CZ parent-company press releases that report combined CZ+SK merchant and volume figures.

brief: Slovakia's non-bank payments layer is enumerable but not measurable: the NBS PSD2 register (with an apparent JSON endpoint), Obchodný register and Register účtovných závierok give a complete, authoritative actor list with statutory financials for every payment institution, EMI and acquirer branch, while FinStat makes that joinable at scale. Actual acquiring data, however, is published only as undated marketing claims by individual players — Global Payments (~37k terminals in SK), SKPAY (~28k POS), Comgate (21k merchants), GoPay (7k), Besteron (1.5k e-shops) — with no provider maintaining a recurring statistical release. The only regular acceptance-side series come from the industry bodies, SBA's card issuing-and-acceptance statistics and ZBK's commentary, amplified by SITA and FinReport, which is also where headline coverage metrics (about 16 terminals per 1,000 inhabitants against an EU average near 32; mobile payments about 22% of card transactions) originate. The practical collection design is therefore: register-driven actor enumeration on a monthly diff, annual text-mining of výročné správy, and periodic snapshotting of acquirer and gateway corporate pages, all normalised against NBS/ECB payment statistics that this pass did not yet cover.
